citation.authors: Kim LEH, Jeong J, Setzer FC, Chung C-H, Jeon HH
citation.title: Cephalometric norms for African Americans with normal occlusion in the Greater Philadelphia region: a retrospective observational study

population.label: African-American
population.region: Greater Philadelphia (University of Pennsylvania orthodontic clinic)

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-13 (norms:compare a vs b exit 1; self-test passed). No mean, SD or n differed on the 36 rows both readers entered. Reader a used the text layer only, so every one of the 37 values was re-read at merge on reader b's page images of Tables 1-5 (PDF pp. 5-6 = pp. 481-482): all agree. Settled: year 2025 (published online 15 Jul 2025; print issue 2026, 87:477-489; a had 2026); 20 definitionMatch differences (a same, b close) settled close where the paper's landmark definitions sit in Supplementary Tables 1-5, not on file (incisor points, occlusal and mandibular planes, gonion, Ricketts points); #33 only b entered it: kept, close (the paper's Ricketts 'Mandibular arc' is Ricketts 1981's 'mandibular bend', p. 130, the catalogue's #33; the catalogue note that left out onfile's 'Mandibular arc (Dr-Xi-Pm)' concerned a separate onfile row, not this angle); #22 FMA 25.2 (Table 1) entered, Downs mandibular plane 25.1 (Table 4) a caveat; Pog-NB -1.2 as printed, sign convention unstated (note); facial angle source Table 4 (b), Table 2's facial depth named in the note. Set-level: selection mixed-occlusion (ruling, P37: the sample is people attending a university orthodontic clinic, p. 480, p. 486; both readers had entered a class-I selection; superseded the same day by owner ruling KIMRANK-1: class-I, ranked as an ordinary Class I sample); modality unknown (a; the films were traced digitally in Dolphin, but the radiograph type is not stated, so b's 'digital' was not kept); authors as printed, Chung C-H (Chun-Hsi).

caveats: Year: published online 15 Jul 2025; printed J Orofac Orthop 2026;87:477-489 (p. 477). The year is 2025 (online first), matching the set id.

Sample (p. 477, p. 480-481): 34 adults (25 F, 9 M) screened from 650 African-American adult records, 2016-2024, at the University of Pennsylvania orthodontic clinic, so they were people attending for orthodontic records (the paper calls them patients seeking treatment, p. 486). Mean age 28.4 ± 12.7 y; no age range given.

Ranked as an ordinary Class I sample (owner ruling KIMRANK-1, 13 Oct; replaces the P37 treatment-sample ruling of the same day): the 34 were chosen for normal occlusion and a balanced profile from records of people attending a university orthodontic clinic, as Cheong 2024 was chosen from clinic patients. So an African-American adult gets this set's adult rows; children keep Bailey & Taylor 1998 and Obamiyi 2019, whose bands cover their ages.

Selection (p. 480): Angle Class I occlusion, overbite 20-30% or >0 and <3 mm, overjet 1-3 mm, no crossbite, minor crowding or spacing/rotations up to 2 mm, and a balanced profile judged by three examiners; no prior orthodontics or orthognathic surgery. Overjet and overbite were explicit numeric inclusion criteria and are not tabled, so nothing is entered for #68/#69 (rule P45).
Only pooled values are tabled; the paper says sex differences were seen but not shown (p. 484).
Traced on Dolphin Imaging 12.0 by one examiner (p. 481); landmark definitions are in Supplementary Tables 1-5, which are not on file, so planes and incisor points cannot be checked.

Not in the catalogue: Maxillary depth 94.1 ± 3.0°, Maxillary height 58.3 ± 3.9°, Facial taper 65.0 ± 4.3°, Corpus length 83.7 ± 5.8 mm, Hinge axis angle 102.4 ± 7.2° (Table 2, p. 481); Anterior cranial base 67.5 ± 4.3 mm, Posterior cranial base 33.1 ± 3.7 mm, Ramus height 45.2 ± 5.9 mm, Mandibular body 73.9 ± 4.8 mm, UFH to LFH 42.1 ± 1.8 %, U1 to FH 122.9 ± 6.6° (Table 3, p. 482).

Not entered (duplicate of an entered catalogue measurement): Downs 'Mandibular plane angle' 25.1 ± 5.6° (Table 4, p. 482) would also be #22, already filled from FMA 25.2 ± 5.6° (Table 1); the 0.1° difference suggests Dolphin drew the two mandibular planes differently, but the paper does not say.
Repeated values printed in more than one table (interincisal, facial angle/facial depth, convexity angle, A to N-Pog, U1 to A-Pog) are entered once, with the other table named in the entry's note.
The 'Published AA norms' column in every table restates other papers (refs 10, 13, 15, 16, 19) and is not entered.
Kim's extraction index (#17), ODI, APDI and combination factor are not given in this paper.
Confidence intervals of the mean are printed beside each value and not entered.
Modality: traced digitally in Dolphin Imaging 12.0 (p. 481); whether the radiographs were digital or scanned film, the machine, the magnification and the head position are not stated.

entries.definitionNote: The paper's row is Ricketts' 'Mandibular arc' with no definition in the main text (Supplementary Tables 1-5 not on file). The catalogue's #33 is the same Ricketts angle: Ricketts 1981 (p. 130) calls it the mandibular bend, the condyle axis (Xi to DC) against the corpus axis (Pm-Xi) extended back. Close, not same, because Dolphin's construction of Xi and DC is not shown. The catalogue's exclusion note on onfile's 'Mandibular arc (Dr-Xi-Pm)' concerned a separate onfile row, not this angle.
entries.note: Adults; the paper gives mean age 28.4 ± 12.7 y and no age range (p. 477, p. 481); upper bound not stated; 40 by convention (rule P18). Against Ricketts 1981's own growth figures (22.0 at 8, about +0.6 per year, p. 130) the expected value near this sample's mean age of 28 is about 34; 35.4 fits.
